column1: # Which released build a generation is swept with (#619, ADR 0073). One row per
# generation that runs a release rather than a build of the checkout; a
# generation with no row here builds the engine from HEAD the way g1 and g2 did.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   generation  tag  asset  sha256
# sha256 is the digest GitHub publishes for the asset, copied here before the
# sweep. This file came with the selection (the first of #619's three merges);
# its readers came with the defines (the second): fetch-engine.sh reads the
# generation's row, fetches the asset, refuses on a mismatch and unpacks it in
# the zig-out layout under spike/unknown-rate/engine/<asset>/ (ignored by git;
# keyed by asset, not tag, so two assets of one tag do not share a directory);
# sweep.sh mounts that
# read-only at /work/zig-out, and apparatus.txt records the pin it checked
# against on a line of its own, beside the banner and the two digest lines the
# container computes from the mounted files; count.py check refuses a complete
# generation that has a row here and no such line.
# The point of a release rather than a HEAD build: the selection is committed
# before any candidate runs, and main moves several times a day, so "the engine
# chosen before the sweep" has to be a thing that does not move with main.
# The architecture is not read from here (#696, ADR 0104). A generation's
# platform is the `machine:` line sweep.sh writes into its apparatus.txt; an
# asset whose name carries an architecture (`-aarch64-linux`, `-x86_64-linux`)
# is held to that line by count.py check, and one that carries none is not
# compared. g4 pins g3's release in its x86_64 build, so the two generations
# differ in the machine and not in the engine.
g3
g4
